      "explanation":"stolen_card",

      "reasoning":"The issuing-country/IP mismatch with failed address verification supports stolen-card use. The failed issuer-authentication and identity check strengthens that explanation, without identifying which component failed."

      "explanation":"new_customer",

      "reasoning":"A legitimate new customer could use a foreign-issued card and encounter an address-verification mismatch. That explanation is weakened by the failed identity check; account youth alone is not adverse evidence."

  "citations":["FP-2 §6.2","R03","FP-2 §6.3","FP-2 §6.4","FP-2 §6.6(b)","FP-2 §5.3(b)","FP-2 §6.5(a)","FP-2 §4.3"],
  "next_check":"none",
  "memo":"R03 holds: the GB-issued card was used from a US IP and AVS failed. Card is the only adverse family; all other rule conditions fail. No household exception applies, and no earlier outcome settles the order. The failed id_check decides under §5.3(b), overriding the ordinary §6.6(b) hold. With Linkage absent, decline is standard and escalation is prohibited. A legitimate new customer using a foreign-issued card is the strongest benign explanation, but it does not override the failed check. The order is unshipped, so decline voids and refunds it and blocks the account. No further check is needed."
